title: Substitutionary Atonement
definition: Substitutionary Atonement is Christ's work of standing in the place of sinners, bearing their guilt, and dying for their sins.
summary: Substitutionary Atonement teaches that Christ made atonement by bearing the guilt and judgment of sinners in their place.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Lamb of God who bears sin and gives His life for His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on the saving meaning of Christ's death: He stands where sinners should have stood and bears what they deserved. It is not merely an example of love or courage, though it is both; it is the atoning sacrifice that reconciles guilty people to God. Substitutionary atonement explains how mercy can be given without justice being denied.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because without substitution the cross loses its saving center. Sinners need more than inspiration; they need guilt removed, wrath satisfied, and peace made. This doctrine keeps the Gospel clear when culture wants a cross without judgment or a Savior without sacrifice.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to the cross as one who needed a Substitute, not merely a teacher. Worship Christ for standing in your place. When preaching or teaching, make clear that Jesus did not simply suffer with sinners—He suffered for sinners.
